title: Bernstein–Vazirani
summary: Recover a whole secret string in one query.
mission: Find the 4-bit secret string s with a single call to oracle(qc): at the end, the input register (qubits 0 to 3) must be in the state |s⟩.

prediction.question: How many queries does a classical algorithm need to find a 4-bit secret string?
prediction.explanation: Each classical query reveals a single bit of s (by querying 0001, 0010, 0100 and 1000), so it takes 4. The quantum algorithm uses one, for any length of s.

hints: The circuit is the same as Deutsch-Jozsa, now with 4 input qubits and the auxiliary on qubit 4.
Auxiliary in |−⟩ with qc.x(4) and qc.h(4); Hadamard on qubits 0 to 3 before and after the oracle.
Use a loop for qubit in range(4): qc.h(qubit). It appears twice, around oracle(qc).
